title: Privacy
description: What Church Hub sends to help us improve it, and how to turn it off.

toggle.label: Share anonymous usage data
toggle.description: Which buttons and pages are used, and the errors that happen. Never your songs, texts, names or files. Applies to every device connected to this app.
toggle.needsPermission: Only someone allowed to edit settings can change this.

policy.title: Privacy policy
policy.intro: Church Hub sends anonymous usage data so we can see how the app is used, find problems and improve it. It cannot tell who you are or which church you are.
policy.device: The operating system and its version, the browser engine and its version, the screen and window size, the app's version and the PostHog library's version.
policy.replay: A recording of the app's screen (session replay), to understand problems. Every text and every field is masked: it shows only grey blocks where words were. Pictures and videos are left out. The projection screens (/screen/…) are never recorded.
policy.why: To learn which features are used and which are not, to find buttons people press but that do not work, and to fix errors before they are reported.
policy.where: To PostHog, in its European Union cloud (Frankfurt, Germany). Nobody else gets it, and it is never sold.
policy.retention: As long as PostHog's plan for the project allows: about one year for events and errors, 30 days for screen recordings. Then it is deleted.
policy.anonymous: Each device gets a random id, and each installation another one; neither is linked to your name, email, computer name or account. No person profiles are created. Your IP address is not stored and is not used to find your location. Web addresses and IP addresses (also local network ones) are removed from everything sent.
policy.never: The text of buttons and pages, song lyrics, Bible verses, programs and their items, anything you type, file and folder names, names, emails and passwords, your IP address or your network's addresses.
policy.feedback: Only when you press Send in Feedback: the app's recent logs (the server's and the desktop app's) are sent privately to the developer under your device's random id, together with the system version and app version, so the problem can be found. Logs can contain file paths and network addresses. This happens even with usage data turned off, because you chose to send it.
policy.off: Turn off "Share anonymous usage data" above. From then on no event, error or screen recording is sent, neither by the app windows nor by the server, on every device connected to this app.

clientEvents.button_pressed: A button, link, menu item, tab or switch was pressed.
clientEvents.shortcut_used: A keyboard shortcut was pressed (never while typing in a field).
clientEvents.startup_failed: The app could not reach its server at start.
clientEvents.$exception: An error in the app: its message, its type and where in the code it happened.
clientEvents.warning: A problem that did not stop the app.
clientEvents.$snapshot: A piece of the masked screen recording.

serverEvents.$exception: An error in the server: its message, its type and where in the code it happened.
serverEvents.$feedback_report: Only when you send feedback: the recent logs (see below).

properties.element: The button's code name (its test id), never its text
properties.container: The code name of the area around the button
properties.role: The kind of element: button, link, tab, switch…
properties.icon: The name of the button's icon (for example trash-2)
properties.feature: The part of the app: songs, bible, schedules…
properties.route: The page's pattern, like /songs/$songId, never the song or the address
properties.shortcut: The key combination, like CommandOrControl+K or ArrowRight
properties.scope: app: pressed in the app; system: pressed in another program
properties.boot_phase: The start step that got stuck
properties.boot_message: The server's message for that step
properties.ever_reachable: Whether the server answered at least once
properties.message: The error or warning message (addresses removed)
properties.source: Which part of the code reported it
properties.report_id: Your device's random id, sent with your feedback
properties.server_log_tail: The end of the server's log
properties.tauri_log_tail: The end of the desktop app's log
